Minute 0:00–1:00 · The question

Where should we investigate first?

The site turns a municipality-level dataset into a transparent screening tool for digital and commercial opportunity across Cabo Verde.

  • 22 municipalities
  • Demographic, employment, education, mobile, and internet indicators
  • A bilingual decision interface
Open overview →

Say: “This is not a prediction engine. It organizes the evidence we have so we can compare places and decide where deeper research should begin.”

01 / 05
Minute 1:00–2:00 · Read the overview

See scale, access, and gaps at a glance

Start with the headline indicators and opportunity bars. The dashboard summarizes population, recorded internet users, internet penetration, and the potential-user gap. The island matrix provides a territorial view without implying a precise map.

Show overviewSwitch PT / EN

Demonstrate: change the chart metric from opportunity score to internet penetration, then point out how the ranking changes because each metric answers a different question.

02 / 05
Minute 2:00–3:00 · Compare evidence

Move from a national view to municipal detail

The ranking can be searched and reordered by opportunity score, population, internet penetration, potential new users, or density. The comparison view places up to three municipalities side by side using the same definitions.

Open site for ranking demo →

Demonstrate: sort the ranking by internet penetration, open one municipal profile, then compare Praia, São Vicente, and Santa Catarina. Explain that ordering by a single metric differs from the composite score.

03 / 05
Minute 3:00–4:00 · Test assumptions

The recommendation changes when priorities change

The simulator combines six normalized components. Users can select a strategy preset, adjust weights, choose a shortlist size, and export the resulting candidates.

  • Market size: 25%
  • Digital gap: 20%
  • Density, employment, conversion: 15% each
  • Education opportunity: 10%
Open simulator →

Demonstrate: switch from “Balanced” to “Digital gap” and show the shortlist changing. This is the key transparency feature: the model exposes judgment instead of hiding it.

04 / 05
Minute 4:00–5:00 · Conclude responsibly

A shortlist is the beginning of a decision

The site supports structured comparison and sensitivity testing. It cannot prove demand, causality, profitability, or project impact. The source year and full provenance are not identified, and key market and cost variables are missing.

Methodology noteEvidence reflectionDownload CSV

Close with: “The responsible use of this tool is to identify where to validate next—by confirming the data, adding coverage and market evidence, and testing findings with local stakeholders.”
